title: Biomechanical study of plantar pressures during walking in male soccer players with increased vs. normal hip alpha angles.
journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine

sections.label: BACKGROUND
sections.text: Femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is accompanied by increased hip alpha angles, in particular in athletes with high impact sports.

sections.label: OBJECTIVE
sections.text: The aim of our study was to investigate the dynamic function of the foot during walking in male soccer players with increased versus normal alpha angles.

sections.label: METHODS
sections.text: Plantar pressures of 20 injury-free male soccer players were recorded during barefoot walking at 1.6 m/s. Ten subjects had bilaterally increased (>55°) (IA) and ten subjects normal (<50°) hip alpha angles (NA). Both standing and kicking leg were analyzed.

sections.label: RESULTS
sections.text: Compared to NA, IA showed lower force-time-integrals (-23%; p< 0.01), pressure-time-integrals (-29%; p< 0.001) and relative loads (p< 0.05) under the heel. In IA contact area of the hallux is about 13% (p< 0.05) reduced. In IA relative loads are increased under the lateral midfoot (p< 0.05) and the second toe (p< 0.05). Higher loading of the lateral midfoot is also reflected in the increased force-time integral (+33%; p< 0.001). No differences between legs and no interactions, indicating a specifity in kicking or standing leg, are found.

sections.label: CONCLUSIONS
sections.text: Compared to NA, soccer players with IA show a forward shifting of the center of pressure which indicates a compensatory mechanism of the foot during walking.
